# checkemail

> checkemail is a free, open-source (MIT) email validation engine by Sai Akash Neela (@saiakashneela). It checks RFC 5321/5322 syntax, DNS A/CNAME and MX records, matches 9,000+ disposable domains, detects role inboxes, canonicalizes aliases (Gmail dots, plus-addressing, pm.me), fingerprints the mail provider and returns a 0-100 confidence score. Zero runtime dependencies. Runs in Node.js 18+ and Bun (npm package `checkemail`), as a Docker HTTP API (`saiakashneela/checkemail`), or on Cloudflare Workers.

Key facts:

- Install: `npm i checkemail` or `bun add checkemail`. Usage: `import { validateEmail } from 'checkemail'; await validateEmail('john.doe+test@gmail.com')`.
- Docker: `docker run -p 3000:3000 saiakashneela/checkemail`, then `GET /validate?email=` and `GET /health`.
- checkemail never sends SMTP probes. It proves the domain can receive mail, not that a specific mailbox exists.
- Statuses: LIKELY, DISPOSABLE, INVALID_DOMAIN, NO_MX_RECORDS, INVALID_FORMAT. Anything other than LIKELY scores 0; a clean personal address scores 90.
- Privacy: validation runs in your own process. Only the domain is sent over the network, as DNS queries.
- The disposable list comes from the disposable-email-domains project and is republished to npm and Docker Hub every Monday and Thursday.

## Docs

- [Full documentation for LLMs](https://checkemail.dev/llms-full.txt): install, API, response fields, statuses, scoring, providers, Docker and Workers deployment, FAQ
- [README](https://github.com/SaiAkashNeela/checkemail-dev#readme): usage and response reference
- [Live demo](https://checkemail.dev/#demo): validate any address in the browser
